Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

SPECIFICATION FOR 
SCOOP, STANLEY BOYD'S PATTERN 



1. Scope — Covers dimensional and other requirements for Stanley Boyd's pattern scoop used in 
general surgery. 

2. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1.

FIG. 1 SCOOP, STANLEY BOYD'S PATTERN 

2.1 Deviation of ± 2*5 percent shall be allowed on all dimensions. 

3. Material — Stainless steel of Designation 40Crl3 of IS : 6603-1972 'Specification for stainless 
steel bars and flats'. 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The scoop shall be free from pits, burrs, scales and other like defects. 

4.2 The lips of the spoon like portion shall be sharp. 

4.3 All other edges shall be rounded off. 

4.4 Suitable grooves for good hold shall be provided in the middle of the scoop. 

4.5 The scoop shall be polished bright and passivated. 

5. Heat Treatment — The scoop shall be hardened and tempered to give a hardness of 520 to 600 HI/.

6. Tests 

6.1 Performance — The lip of each spoon shall be made to scrape vigorously over the surface of a fresh 
piece of bone applying maximum pressure. At the end of the test, the lip of the scoop shall not show 
any distortion or blunting. 

6.2 Flexibility — The scoop shall be ffx^d in a vice such that the large spoon lies between the jaws of 
the vice and the rest of the scoop protrudes above the vice. By the application of a force at the upper 
extremity of the small spoon, the shaft Jhall be deflected in a direction perpendicular to the axis of the 
shaft and at right angles to the long axis of the jaws of the vice by 1 5 mm as measured at the level of 
upper extremity of the small spoon. On release of the force, no permanent set shall be observed. 

6.2,1 The test shall be repeated with the small spoon fixed in the vice and the shaft projecting above 
the vice. The deflecting force shall be applied to the large spoon at a point 200 mm above the upper 
surface of the vice. The shaft shall be deflected by 20 mm as measured at the level of the point where 
the force is applied. On release of the force, no permanent set shall be observed. 

6.3 Corrosion Resistance Test — The instrument shall show no sign of corrosion when put to boiling and 
autociaving test in accordance with 13:7531-1975 'Method for boiling and autoclaving test for 
corrosion resistance of stainless steel surgical instruments'. 

7. Marking — The scoop shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the following: 

a) Manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark; and 

b) The words 'Stainless Steel' or the letters 'SS'. 

7.1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. Packing — As agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.
